doc.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Sixties: Verve end, California, Half Note, Duets
title: Making the 'Duets' album
summary: He recalls how he picked partners, smoking on the date, tenor with Elvin Jones, and Ray Nance and Jim Hall.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Let’s talk about the Duets album from sixty-seven. This is your first major record after Motion. This is part of the beginnings of Milestone Records that Dick Katz and Orrin Keepnews started . . . That was an important record for them. That got a lot of attention and for you as well.

I think it was mine and [I] was probably encouraged by Dick Katz. We had scheduled it on the hour and on the half hour. Each situation didn’t last more than half an hour and I’d say “next” and Elvin would come up or whatever . . . Eddie Gomez had some, ladies and gentlemen, Eddie Gomez had some pot and I smoked some pot on that record and it was nice. It was so nice that I played a duet with Elvin Jones on tenor. I took the tenor off the shelf in the closet . . .
[Laughing] Yeah. That stuff works you know what I’m saying?
It’s a good sounding duet, too.

I was very pleased with it. I said “Jesus, don’t sound like Coltrane but [it] sounds interesting” I thought. There were all those nice situations like I had decided that I just wanted to get to play duets with people and I called different people, unlikely people, like Ray Nance and he was quite nice about it and when I suggested playing . . . Marshall Brown said “You know, if you’re playing with Ray Nance, play a Duke Ellington song or something like that.” I said “Do you want to try something free?” and wham, he was into it. And at the record date, I went “da da” and he went to the next movement.
That’s the most unexpected thing on the whole record, that duet with Ray. He’s the last person you would’ve expected to do a free thing.
He was right in there. I did a little tenor and guitar thing with Jim Hall that was kind of nice.
